transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jon Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (AuroraCloud PM), Liu Chen (AuroraCloud Integration Eng), Diego Marquez (AuroraCloud Marketplace Ops)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for the joint solution (AuroraCloud marketplace + Redwood inference), packaging steps for the AuroraCloud marketplace SKU, and to schedule hands-on validation. Primary ask: make sure network/topology and auth (SSO, KMS) details are clear so Redwood can produce a reference arch and Aurora can prepare the listing assets.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're on the 15:00 slot, i'll kick us off. maya from redwood, ae on this account, with jon who's our se. could you do quick intros priya?
[00:08] Priya: yeah hi all, priya here partner pm at auroracloud, diego helps with marketplace ops and liu is our integration engineer. excited to sync on the joint solution.
[00:18] Jon: cool, hi, jon rivera se at redwood. we'll try to keep this technical but pragmatic, focus on the listing, the reference arch and what we need to validate.
[00:26] Diego: quick note, our marketplace has a couple of SKU types, one is a managed listing, the other is a bring-your-own infra listing, so we want to decide which model works for redwood.
[00:38] Maya: yeah right, and redwood supports three deployment modes so there's a natural mapping: hosted api -> managed listing, dedicated/reserved -> marketplace reserved capacity, and private -> bring-your-own. we should pick the primary pattern for the first listing.
[00:53] Priya: for go-to-market speed, managed listing with a marketplace billing integration is easier, but we need to confirm compliance bits - soc2, audit logs, and key management notes.
[01:05] Jon: on the security side we have SOC 2 Type 2, optional KMS integration and we can support customer-managed keys for private deployments. small nit: sometimes our docs call it Redwood Dedicate but should be Redwood Dedicated, sorry the auto-transcripts are messy.
[01:22] Liu: ok on network: if we do managed listing, what's the recommended connection? are you doing V P C peering, private link, or public egress with mTLS?
[01:33] Jon: good q. for the managed hosted api we primarily use secure public endpoints with mTLS optional; for dedicated and private we do VPC peering or PrivateLink equivalence. recommended reference arch will show all three. note: we use K V cache and prefix caching optimizations, so low latency paths are recommended for high throughput.
[01:55] Diego: marketplace ops: for our SKU we need a short description, security attestations, a reference arch diagram (SVG + PNG), install scripts if applicable, pricing tiers, and support contacts. also icons and screenshots.
[02:10] Maya: i'll send the marketplace asset checklist, sample descriptions and a few example listings. that'll help speed the packaging.
[02:16] Priya: perfect. technical question — in dedicated mode what are the minimum GPU requirements you're recommending? some of our customers ask for sizing guidance.
[02:26] Jon: for small POCs 1-2 A100-equivalent cards with 32g each is a common starting point; for production, depends on concurrency and sequence length, but we usually show example configs: 4 x A100-80g or 8 x A10g for cost-optimized. will add a sizing table in the ref arch doc.
[02:46] Priya: ok great.
[02:48] [02:48] Liu: on auth flows — if a customer uses auroracloud IAM, how do we integrate? can your control plane federate to SAML or OIDC?
[03:00] Jon: yes we support SAML S S O and OIDC; in private deployments the customer can point our control plane to their IdP or we can stand up a private control plane inside their V P C. we'll include SSO diagrams.
[03:15] Priya: what about audit logs and retention windows? marketplace requires 90 day retention, sometimes longer.
[03:23] Maya: we have configurable retention and can export logs to the customer's S3 or to auroracloud logging. we'll call out default retention and options in the listing.
[03:34] Diego: packaging question — does redwood provide an automated installer for private/on-prem? our marketplace supports both images and helm charts.
[03:43] Jon: we have helm charts and a k8s operator for private deployments; for on-prem we provide a tarball + install script. we'll surface the helm chart in the artifact list.
[03:56] Priya: nice. any concerns about licensing or metering? marketplace needs metering integration for usage-based billing.
[04:05] Maya: hosted API usage is metered per token/embedding; we can provide usage endpoints and billing callbacks for managed listings. for dedicated/reserved there are contract SKUs. we'll document the endpoints.
[04:20] Liu: for integration testing, we want to run a joint validation that hits the API from inside our infra to test latency and auth flows. what do you need from us?
[04:30] Jon: access to a test V P C with a couple test nodes, and ideally a sample model workload or a synthetic load generator. we'll run smoke tests for latency, throughput and kv cache behavior.
[04:44] Diego: we can spin up a test VPC and share temporary creds. timeline?
[04:49] Maya: aim for the week of 6/1, that gives us time to exchange assets now.
[04:54] [05:00] Priya: quick product/marketing ask — we'll want a joint solution blurb of ~150 words and 2-3 screenshots for the listing. can redwood produce that or do you want aurora to draft?
[05:12] Maya: redwood can draft the blurb, but let's collaborate; priya you can provide the go-to-market angle and logos.
[05:19] Priya: will do.
[05:22] Jon: from a technical doc perspective i'll include the following in the ref arch: network/topology, auth flows (SAML/OIDC/KMS), deployment variants, sizing table, example terraform snippets and a smoke test plan.
[05:37] Liu: terraform snippets are great, we use terraform for marketplace packaging.
[05:41] Jon: note — some of the infra folks might call KMS H S M or cloud KMS; we'll keep language generic and add cloud-specific notes for Aurora.
[05:51] Diego: one small policy thing — our marketplace requires that any marketplace listing must pass a security review before publishing; that review takes ~5 business days. do you have a security self-assessment?
[06:04] Maya: yes we have a security questionnaire and SOC 2 report; i'll attach a redacted SOC 2 and the questionnaire responses to the asset bundle.
[06:13] Priya: awesome.
[06:15] [06:20] Jon: ok on integration details — when we do the networking diagram, we'll show optional PrivateLink, VPC peering and a public endpoint with mTLS. also call out expectations around egress IPs so customers can whitelist.
[06:34] Liu: how stable are egress IPs for hosted? sometimes customers need static whitelists.
[06:40] Jon: hosted endpoints are behind a pool of egress IPs per region; for strict whitelisting we recommend dedicated/reserved or private deployments. we'll list both options.
[06:51] Priya: next — can we do an initial compatibility matrix for supported models/quantizations on aurora infra? we have multiple instance types.
[07:02] Jon: yes, i'll include recommended model variants per GPU class (FP16, INT8 quant, etc) and note which kernels we prefer. it's high-level guidance not a certification matrix.
[07:16] Diego: will you provide a small test harness we can run? like a curl example and a small node/python script?
[07:23] Jon: yes, we'll include cURL, python and terraform examples in a repo.
[07:30] Priya: timeline recap — maya, you'll share asset checklist 5/21; liu create test V P C by 5/25; diego will validate SKU packaging 5/24; jon produce ref arch 5/28; run validation week of 6/1. does that sound right?
[07:46] Maya: yup that's our plan.
[07:49] Liu: one last technical item — for telemetry, can you forward per-route latency metrics to aurora monitoring? we have a partner telemetry ingestion endpoint.
[07:59] Jon: we can push metrics via a secure webhook or export to a cloud metric sink; we'll need the endpoint and auth method. we'll also provide per-token cost breakdown in the console.
[08:13] Priya: ok.
[08:15] Diego: question on billing for managed listing: do you support marketplace invoicing flow or do we bill and pay redwood?
[08:25] Maya: we can support marketplace billing for managed listings via billing callbacks, or direct billing for reserved capacity. we'll outline both in the doc.
[08:36] Priya: perfect.
[08:38] [08:40] Jon: any blockers from aurora side for us to proceed?
[08:45] Priya: nothing blocking, just need the asset checklist and the ref arch draft to proceed with marketplace ops.
[08:53] Diego: also need the security questionnaire answers.
[08:56] Maya: i'll attach them.
[08:59] Jon: i'll start the ref arch and share a draft in the repo.
[09:04] Priya: ok let's recap action items and owners in the notes.
[09:10] Maya: recap — i'll send the checklist + SOC2 redaction by 5/21, jon will share ref arch by 5/28, liu will stand up test vpc by 5/25, diego to verify SKU packaging by 5/24, priya confirm marketing/PR timeline by 6/02. schedule the validation week of 6/1.
[09:29] Liu: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:31] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with the repo link and calendar invite for the validation window. bye.

Notes / Links mentioned:
- Redwood marketplace asset checklist (to be shared by Maya)
- Reference architecture repo (Jon will create, link to be shared)
- Security questionnaire and redacted SOC2 (Maya)
- Aurora test VPC details (Liu)

End of transcript.
